atoms.canonical_statement: The study proposes AUGUST, a sequential question-answering framework intended to model hierarchical and conditional gastric pathology diagnostic reasoning.
The study used 23,072 gastric whole-slide images spanning up to 19 hierarchical diagnostic tasks and 79,924 question-answer pairs across training and validation datasets.
AUGUST performs diagnosis as a sequence of context-aware questions, question-conditioned WSI projections, and pathway-constrained answers in which each answer determines the next diagnostic task.
The diagnostic taxonomy is organized into coarse-, fine-, and grading-level tasks across anatomical location, H. pylori infection status, and pathologic condition.
Auto-QA evaluates fully autonomous hierarchical inference with downstream tasks conditioned on upstream model predictions, thereby retaining cascade-error propagation.

HITL-QA replaces incorrect upstream model predictions with ground-truth labels before downstream inference to emulate expert confirmation or correction and isolate downstream task capability from cascade errors.
GastUJB-Train contains 6,913 WSIs and 27,069 question-answer pairs and covers 3 coarse-level, 11 fine-level, and 5 grading-level tasks.
GastUJB-Test contains 5,166 WSIs and 21,396 question-answer pairs and serves as the internal validation cohort.
GastAIHub contains 6,360 gastric WSIs after exclusions and serves as a multi-institutional external validation cohort.
GastAIHub excluded non-gastric-biopsy slides, gastric non-epithelial neoplasms outside the diagnostic taxonomy, and slides with missing or unreliable diagnostic information.
GastCODiPAI combines 2,995 stomach-biopsy and 647 stomach-endoscopic-resection specimens for a total of 3,642 WSIs from a consortium of 15 university hospitals.
GastADC22 contains 991 surgical gastric adenocarcinoma WSIs, each from a distinct patient, and was re-annotated to the study taxonomy.
For each sample, the study assigns a single coarse-level condition label based on the lesion of highest clinical significance when multiple pathologies coexist.
Inflammatory disease is the only multi-label fine-level condition task and includes chronic inflammation, neutrophilic activity, glandular atrophy, intestinal metaplasia, erosion, and ulceration.

Chronic inflammation and neutrophilic activity grading were excluded from evaluation because their grading annotations were not consistently documented and were considered substantially missing or unreliable.
Dysplasia grading uses three labels: indefinite for dysplasia, low-grade dysplasia, and high-grade dysplasia.

Adenocarcinoma grading merges poorly differentiated, poorly cohesive, and signet-ring-cell categories into a single poorly cohesive category, yielding three grades: well differentiated, moderately differentiated, and poorly cohesive.
WSIs are segmented for tissue and tessellated into non-overlapping 512×512-pixel patches at 20× magnification.
Patch-level representations are extracted with the frozen UNI ViT-Large pathology encoder, and baseline methods use the same precomputed frozen features and dataset splits.
AUGUST uses S4MIL as a parametric slide-level aggregation layer to summarize patch embeddings and question context into a compact slide-level representation.
The question-aware fusion adapter explicitly combines the slide embedding with the current question embedding and projects the result into the LLM embedding space.
ME-LLaMA3 is used for both question encoding and language-model decoding so that question embeddings and generative diagnostic reasoning share the same semantic space.

Structured prompts specify the clinical question, a fixed output template, an explicit candidate label set when applicable, and optional domain context; target answers instantiate the same template with the ground-truth label.
Single-VQA consists of task-specific single-turn question-answer pairs designed to teach task-relevant evidence selection, output formatting, and valid-label selection.
WSI-VQA uses a fixed whole-slide diagnosis question and a structured answer aggregating all ground-truth labels to align slide representations with the LLM space.
Multi-VQA orders task-specific question-answer pairs along the diagnostic hierarchy so that each turn is conditioned on the accumulated prior question-answer history.
The training objective combines autoregressive generation loss, supervised label-token classification loss, answer-margin loss, and auxiliary coarse-level classification loss.
Training uses three sequential sessions: cross-domain WSI-VQA alignment, Single-VQA visual instruction tuning, and Multi-VQA training for hierarchy-consistent multi-turn reasoning.
Class imbalance is addressed with inverse-frequency importance sampling and feature-level augmentation including stochastic patch-embedding dropout, block erasure, and minority-class mixing.
MIL baselines are adapted to the same coarse-to-fine hierarchy by replacing their final single-task heads with hierarchical multi-task heads and using identical Auto-QA and HITL-QA selection rules.
The baseline set includes ABMIL, TransMIL, CLAM-SB, S4MIL, DTFDMIL, TITAN, PRISM, SlideChat, and WSICaption.
Experiments used two NVIDIA A6000 GPUs; MIL baselines were trained for 40 epochs with Adam, learning rate 1e-4, weight decay 1e-5, and batch size 1.
Under Auto-QA, AUGUST produced the highest structured-report scores across all five BLEU1–4 and ROUGEL metrics on the internal GastUJB cohort.
On GastUJB structured report generation, AUGUST achieved BLEU4 of 82.29, exceeding the representative MIL, VLM, and FM baselines.
On GastUJB structured report generation, AUGUST achieved ROUGEL of 92.32, exceeding the representative MIL, VLM, and FM baselines.
On GastAIHub structured report generation, AUGUST achieved the highest ROUGEL score (91.80).
On GastCODiPAI structured report generation, AUGUST achieved the highest ROUGEL score (90.97).
On GastADC22 structured report generation, AUGUST achieved the highest ROUGEL score (84.29).
Under Auto-QA, AUGUST achieved an average task-level F1 score of 0.780 on GastUJB.
Under Auto-QA, AUGUST achieved an average task-level F1 score of 0.780 on GastAIHub.
Under Auto-QA, AUGUST achieved an average task-level F1 score of 0.703 on GastCODiPAI.
Under Auto-QA, AUGUST achieved an average task-level F1 score of 0.625 on GastADC22.
Aggregated across datasets and tasks under Auto-QA, AUGUST achieved an average F1 score of 0.722 (95% CI 0.696–0.747), higher than the best MIL, VLM, and FM family baselines.

atoms.canonical_statement: On GastUJB, AUGUST had a median task F1 of 0.802 with IQR 0.163, compared with Best MIL median 0.735 with IQR 0.226.
For the coarse condition task on GastUJB, AUGUST achieved F1 0.879 versus 0.876 for Best MIL, 0.827 for Best VLM, and 0.506 for Best FM.
Across all cohorts, HITL-QA improved AUGUST performance by an average of 0.021 F1 relative to Auto-QA.

On GastUJB Auto-QA, AUGUST achieved F1 0.357 for glandular atrophy, a task that remained lower-performing than many other diagnostic tasks.
On GastUJB Auto-QA, AUGUST achieved F1 0.577 for ulceration, a task that remained lower-performing than many other diagnostic tasks.
On GastUJB Auto-QA, AUGUST achieved F1 0.689 for erosion, a task that remained lower-performing than many other diagnostic tasks.
For adenocarcinoma grading under Auto-QA, AUGUST achieved F1 0.728 on GastUJB.
For adenocarcinoma grading under Auto-QA, AUGUST achieved F1 0.619 on GastAIHub.
For adenocarcinoma grading under Auto-QA, AUGUST achieved F1 0.646 on GastCODiPAI.
For adenocarcinoma grading under Auto-QA, AUGUST achieved F1 0.607 on GastADC22.
Training-versus-test analysis showed a pronounced generalization gap for data-scarce classes, with near-perfect training accuracy but substantially lower test accuracy for rare lesions.

Grad-CAM review indicated that correct AUGUST predictions generally emphasized diagnostically plausible tissue regions, while representative misclassifications showed attention that missed or diffusely covered relevant morphology.
Across major disease-category tasks, AUGUST had a mean false-negative rate of 32.04% under Auto-QA versus 37.10% for Best MIL.
Across major disease-category tasks, AUGUST had a mean false-negative rate of 25.49% under HITL-QA versus 29.84% for Best MIL.
On GastAIHub, AUGUST had an H. pylori-positive false-negative rate of 13.06% versus 42.04% for Best MIL.
On GastAIHub, AUGUST had a condition-level cancer false-negative rate of 26.61% versus 41.75% for Best MIL.
Removing both visual-instruction and multi-turn training sessions reduced mean Auto-QA F1 from 0.751 to 0.554.
Removing both visual-instruction and multi-turn training sessions reduced mean HITL-QA F1 from 0.772 to 0.595.
Without data augmentation, AUGUST mean F1 declined to 0.613 under Auto-QA and 0.721 under HITL-QA.
Simultaneously removing the LLM and hierarchical constraints reduced mean Auto-QA F1 from 0.751 to 0.559 and HITL-QA F1 from 0.772 to 0.666.

atoms.canonical_statement: Removing H. pylori status as contextual information reduced overall average F1 from 0.755 to 0.717.
The authors conclude that explicit clinically ordered, conditional reasoning improves hierarchical gastric pathology diagnosis compared with disconnected task optimization.
The authors state that no evaluated system is yet capable of fully autonomous and clinically safe gastric WSI diagnosis and that human oversight remains necessary.

The discussion proposes an autonomous pre-read followed by expert review as the most realistic high-throughput deployment pattern, with exception-based or checkpoint HITL review for selected high-impact decisions.

For safer deployment, the authors recommend uncertainty display, links to supporting visual evidence, explicit upstream override with downstream recomputation, user training, and periodic feedback and audit cycles.
Training and validation data are imbalanced and rare subtypes remain difficult, limiting performance on data-scarce classes.
Although the study includes external validation, the authors note that real-world variability may be broader and call for prospective multi-site validation and domain adaptation or fine-tuning.
Question-answer prompt templates were manually designed, which limits scalability and transfer to other organs or disease settings.
Assigning a single coarse condition label based on the lesion of highest clinical significance may under-represent the complexity of WSIs containing multiple concurrent lesions.
Grad-CAM validation is qualitative and does not provide formal quantitative agreement with expert-annotated pathological evidence.
The current hierarchy uses hard thresholding and lacks an uncertainty-aware mechanism for ambiguous predictions or uncertainty propagation across dependent steps.
AUGUST requires comparatively greater computational resources, which may limit practicality in some real-world settings.
Retrospective benchmark performance does not establish clinical utility; the authors state that prospective multi-reader multi-case studies with a dedicated clinical interface are needed.
GastUJB-Train, GastUJB-Test, GastAIHub, GastCODiPAI, and GastADC22 are reported as publicly available through the cited repositories or data portals.
The authors report that code and implementation details are available in the AUGUST GitHub repository.
The work was supported by the National Research Foundation of Korea, the Hyundai Motor Chung Mong-Koo Foundation Global Scholarship, and the Catholic Medical Center Research Foundation.
